items.detail: Independent bias audit within 1 year before use, public audit summary on the careers site, and notice at least 10 business days before use describing the qualifications and characteristics assessed and how to request an alternative process or accommodation.

items.text: California CRD ADS rules and CCPA ADMT
items.detail: CRD (from 1 Oct 2025): discriminatory ADS outcomes violate FEHA, vendors can be the employer's agents, anti-bias testing is relevant evidence, ADS data is kept 4 years, and tools must not screen out people with disabilities without accommodation. CCPA: a risk assessment before processing, and from 1 Jan 2027 pre-use ADMT notice, an opt-out or human appeal, and access to information about the ADMT logic for significant employment decisions.

items.text: Colorado SB 26-189 (from 1 Jan 2027)
items.detail: Pre-use notice of ADMT in consequential employment decisions, a plain-language explanation within 30 days of an adverse decision, and rights to correct data and ask for human review; developers supply documentation. AG enforcement with a 60-day cure period.

items.text: EU AI Act (Germany)
items.detail: Emotion recognition at work has been banned since Feb 2025 and the AI literacy duty already applies. Employment uses listed in Annex III are high-risk, with deployer duties (human oversight, logging, input data quality, informing worker representatives and affected workers) from 2 Dec 2027 under the Digital Omnibus (Reg. (EU) 2026/1744).

items.text: Other AI and biometric laws
items.detail: Illinois AI notice (HB 3773, from 1 Jan 2026); Texas TRAIGA ban on intentional discrimination; Ontario AI disclosure in job postings; PIPL Art. 24 transparency and right to refuse automated decisions; biometric laws (Illinois BIPA, Texas CUBI, WA RCW 19.375, Colorado C.R.S. 6-1-1314).

items.text: Germany works council
items.detail: Any tool that can monitor behaviour or performance is co-determined (§87(1) no.6 BetrVG), AI selection guidelines need consent (§95(2a)), and the council may bring in an AI expert at company cost (§80(3)). Record the date the council was informed and the date the works agreement was signed or amended; no go-live before agreement.

items.text: Other employee representation
items.detail: Israel: consult the union where a collective agreement applies. Vietnam: dialogue with the grassroots union and monitoring rules in the internal labour regulations. China and Taiwan: handbook or work-rule changes adopted through the required procedure.

items.text: Candidate and employee notices, and where each is published
items.detail: CCPA notice at collection; NYC 10-business-day notice; Ontario posting disclosure; Illinois AI notice; GDPR Arts. 13-14; PIPL separate notice and consent; PDPL Art. 25; Israel Amendment 13 notice; Colorado pre-use notice from 2027.

items.text: Accessibility and alternatives
items.detail: An accommodation route for anyone who can't use the tool (ADA, AODA) and an alternative process or human review on request.

items.text: Impact assessments completed, with dates and approvers
items.detail: GDPR Art. 35 DPIA, China PIPIA, Vietnam DPIA filed within 60 days, CCPA risk assessment, Quebec PIA. Attach each one.

items.text: Data processing agreement: roles, purpose limits, confidentiality, sub-processor approval and flow-down, audit rights, and local terms (GDPR Art. 28, PIPL entrusted-processing contract, PDPL, DPDP processor clauses).
Transfer clauses and filings are in place before any data flows (SCCs, China standard contract, Vietnam transfer impact assessment).
CCPA service-provider terms: no selling or sharing, no training on our data, and deletion at exit with a certificate.

AI terms: documentation and model cards, notice of material model changes, cooperation with bias testing and audits, decision logs kept 4 years for California, and support for adverse-decision explanations.
Security: breach notice within 24-48 hours, agreed security standards, penetration testing, insurance, and indemnity for regulatory fines and third-party claims where negotiable.
DOJ Data Security Program representations: no covered-person access to bulk US sensitive personal data, and notice of any ownership change.
Trade Compliance has cleared any vendor access to technical data (e.g., engineering project or performance data containing controlled technology).
Risk rating: Low / Medium / High
items.detail: High: automated employment decisions, monitoring, biometrics, sensitive data, China or Vietnam transfers, or DOJ Data Security Program exposure.

items.text: Approvals and dates
items.detail: HR business owner; Privacy; Information Security; Legal (employment); Trade Compliance (technical data); works council (Germany); AI governance committee (high-risk tools).

items.text: Conditions of approval and go-live checklist
items.detail: Notices published, filings made, reviewers trained on the human-review workflow, bias baseline captured.

items.text: Re-assessment date
items.detail: Every year for high-risk tools, and at renewal or any material change (a new AI feature, country or sub-processor).

notes: Assess the use case, not just the vendor: the same product can be low-risk for interview scheduling and high-risk for ranking candidates.
AI features switched on inside existing systems are the most common way unassessed AI enters HR, so they go through this form too.
The employer stays liable for discriminatory outcomes even when the vendor built the model (CRD agent rules, Title VII disparate impact), so insist on bias-testing data and run our own.
Keep a person with real authority and time in every consequential decision, and log overrides. Rubber-stamping isn't human review.
China and Vietnam transfer filings and German works agreements take months; start them at the pilot stage, not at go-live.
File the completed form, impact assessments and approvals in the POL-50 AI tool inventory, and re-assess on every material change.

countryNotes.us: NYC Local Law 144 requires an annual independent bias audit, a published summary and 10 business days' notice before an AEDT is used, and Illinois requires notice of AI use. The DOJ Data Security Program (28 CFR 202) restricts vendor agreements that give covered persons access to bulk US sensitive personal data.
countryNotes.us-ca: CRD ADS rules (from 1 Oct 2025) make discriminatory ADS outcomes FEHA violations, treat vendors as agents and require 4-year retention of ADS data. CCPA risk assessments apply now, and ADMT pre-use notice, opt-out or appeal and access duties start on 1 Jan 2027.
countryNotes.us-co: SB 26-189 (from 1 Jan 2027) requires pre-use ADMT notice, a plain-language explanation within 30 days of an adverse decision, correction and human review, with AG enforcement and a 60-day cure period. Biometric tools also need the C.R.S. 6-1-1314 policy and consent.
countryNotes.us-nc: There is no AI-in-employment statute. Require vendor breach notice fast enough for the company to meet G.S. 75-65, and secure disposal (G.S. 75-64).
countryNotes.us-tx: TRAIGA (from 1 Jan 2026) bans deploying AI with intent to discriminate; document each tool's purpose, testing and safeguards (NIST AI RMF alignment helps), and check biometric features for CUBI consent.
countryNotes.us-wa: There is no AI-in-employment statute as of Sept 2026, but WLAD disparate impact and the biometric law (RCW 19.375) apply, and audio features need all-party consent. Expect 2027 bills following the AG's AI Task Force report.
countryNotes.ca: Ontario job postings must disclose AI use in screening, assessment or selection (since 1 Jan 2026), and BC PIPA requires notice of purposes. Quebec Law 25 requires a PIA before transfers outside Quebec and notice of decisions based solely on automated processing.
countryNotes.de: Any tool that can monitor behaviour or performance, including AI features switched on later, is co-determined (§87(1) no.6 BetrVG); run a DPIA, sign an Art. 28 DPA and cover US transfers. Under the AI Act, emotion recognition at work is banned, AI literacy applies now, and Annex III deployer duties start on 2 Dec 2027.
countryNotes.il: Assess vendors against Amendment 13, the outsourcing rules in the Data Security Regulations 2017 and the Transfer Abroad Regulations 2001; the Privacy Protection Authority treats AI systems as fully subject to privacy law. Monitoring features must pass the Isakov proportionality test.
countryNotes.in: Until DPDP duties start on 13 May 2027, the SPDI Rules require written consent for sensitive data and reasonable security; write DPDP processor obligations into contracts now. CERT-In's 6-hour incident reporting covers vendor incidents affecting Indian systems.
countryNotes.tw: Disclose vendor processing and cross-border transfers in the PDPA notice, bind vendors to security maintenance measures, and get written consent or a statutory basis for health and other sensitive data.
countryNotes.cn: Entrusted processing, automated decision-making and cross-border transfers each need a PIPIA kept for 3 years, and transfers need the HR-management exemption, a standard contract filing, certification or a CAC assessment depending on volume. Facial recognition needs separate consent and a non-biometric alternative.
countryNotes.vn: File or update the DPIA within 60 days of starting processing, and file a transfer impact assessment with the Ministry of Public Security unless the ILR-based HR-management exemption applies. Disclose monitoring and automated tools to employees (PDPL Art. 25); biometric data is sensitive.

templates.name: HR data subject request response checklist
templates.purpose: Takes the HR privacy desk through an employee's, applicant's or former employee's request to access, correct, delete or restrict their data, from identity verification to secure delivery. It sets the local deadline at intake and makes sure exemptions and redactions are applied consistently and documented.
templates.audience: The HR data subject request desk (Privacy Office and People Operations), HR Technology and system owners (searches), Legal (exemptions and disputes), Employee Relations (investigation files).
templates.when: Opened the day a request arrives through any channel (it doesn't need to cite a law), including personnel-file and payroll-record requests. Deadlines run from receipt.
templates.owner: Privacy Office with People Operations (HR data subject request desk)

items.text: Log the request in the DSAR tracker on the day it arrives: requester, date received, channel and request type (access or copy, correction, deletion, restriction or objection, portability, consent withdrawal, ADMT or sale/sharing opt-out, personnel file, payroll records, discharge-reason statement).
Treat any request as valid, whatever its wording or channel (an email to a manager, an HR ticket, a lawyer's letter); managers and HRBPs forward it to the desk within 1 business day.

Verify identity proportionately: current employees through SSO or an HRIS login; former employees and applicants by matching 2-3 data points already held. Don't ask for more data than needed, or for ID copies unless there is no alternative.
Agents and lawyers: get the requester's signed authorization (CCPA authorized agents; lawyers' letters are common in disputes in Germany and Israel).
Ask for clarification only where the request is genuinely unclear, and record the date; don't assume the clock stops meanwhile (verify local rules).

Flag disputes: if the requester has a claim, dispute or investigation open, involve Legal before responding. California can refuse personnel-file inspection once the employee has sued over a personnel matter (LC 1198.5(n)).

sections.title: Log & clock
sections.intro: Set the deadline at intake from where the requester works and lives. Where several regimes apply, use the shortest.

items.text: California CCPA (employees, applicants, contractors): confirm receipt within 10 business days and respond within 45 calendar days, extendable once by 45 with notice.

California personnel file (LC 1198.5): inspection or copies within 30 days (up to 35 by agreement), now including training records (SB 513). Payroll records (LC 226): within 21 days. Signed employment instruments: a copy on request (LC 432). Penalties are $750.

Washington: free personnel-file copies and a signed discharge-reason statement within 21 days (HB 1308). Colorado: personnel-file inspection at least once a year (C.R.S. 8-2-129). North Carolina and Texas: no statutory right; respond under policy within 30 days.

Canada: PIPEDA 30 days, extendable by 30 with notice; BC PIPA 30 days (verify business-day counting), extendable. Ontario private-sector employees have no statutory right, so apply the 30-day standard; Quebec Law 25 covers Quebec staff.
Germany (GDPR): 1 month from receipt, extendable by 2 months for complex or numerous requests, with notice and reasons inside the first month. Personnel-file inspection under §83 BetrVG on request.
China (PIPL Arts. 44-47, 50): no fixed statutory deadline, so target 15 working days (verify) and give reasons for any refusal.
India: a grievance officer under the SPDI Rules now; from 13 May 2027, DPDP Act rights of access, correction, erasure and grievance redressal, answered within 90 days.
Taiwan (PDPA): access and copies within 15 days, correction or deletion within 30 days, each extendable once by the same period with written reasons (verify).
Vietnam (PDPL, Decree 356): acknowledge within 2 working days, then complete access or correction within 10 days, restriction or consent withdrawal within 15, and deletion within 20.
Israel (Protection of Privacy Law ss.13-14): respond within the regulatory period (30 days, extendable; verify). Amendment 13 adds statutory damages for some failures.

Map the request to systems: Darwinbox (HRIS), Greenhouse (ATS), payroll providers, benefits and equity administrators, the LMS, performance and engagement tools, ER and hotline case management, IT tickets, badge logs, email and chat, shared drives, the EHS incident system.
Send search instructions to system owners with a 5-business-day deadline, and record who searched what, when and with which terms.
Include data held by processors (payroll, benefits, background checks, AI and assessment vendors) and request their extracts under the DPA.

For email and chat, run targeted searches (name, employee ID, email aliases, nicknames) over the relevant period, and record why the search was proportionate. GDPR requires a reasonable and proportionate search, not every mention.
CCPA responses cover data collected since 1 Jan 2022 unless that is impossible or disproportionate, and include categories, sources, purposes and recipients as well as the data itself.
Collate and de-duplicate results in a restricted review folder with access logging.

Third-party data: redact other people's personal data (names, contact details, opinions about them) unless they consent or disclosure is reasonable, and never reveal complainants or witnesses in investigation files (GDPR Art. 15(4); BDSG §29; CCPA).
Privilege: withhold attorney-client privileged and work-product material and log it; Legal decides.

Investigations and legal claims: withhold or delay material whose release would prejudice an open investigation, legal claim or law-enforcement matter, where local law allows (CCPA legal-claims exception; BDSG §34; PIPEDA s.9(3); verify elsewhere).

California personnel-file exclusions (LC 1198.5): records of an investigation into a possible criminal offense, letters of reference, and pre-employment ratings or reports. Where both the personnel-file right and CCPA apply, give the broader response.

Trade secrets and confidential business information (compensation models, pay-range tools, security logs, export-controlled technical data) are withheld or summarized, while the requester's own data within them is disclosed.

Deletion: apply retention and legal-hold exceptions (payroll, tax, I-9, OSHA, EEO and ADS records, and statutory retention elsewhere), delete what isn't needed, and tell the requester what was kept and why.

Correction: fix factual errors. For disputed opinions such as ratings or investigation findings, add the employee's statement rather than rewrite the record (Washington and Germany give rebuttal rights).
Any refusal or partial refusal is documented with its legal basis and reviewed by Legal, and the response gives the reason and, where required, how to complain to the regulator.

Dear [Name], We received your request of [date] to [access / correct / delete] your personal information. We have searched [systems] and enclose [a copy of your personal information / confirmation of the changes made]. [We have withheld or redacted [description] because [legal basis, e.g., it contains other people's personal information / it is legally privileged / it relates to an ongoing investigation].]

We use your information for [purposes]. We obtained it from [sources], share it with [categories of recipients, including service providers in [countries]] and keep it for [retention period or criteria]. You also have the right to [correct / delete / restrict / object / withdraw consent / appeal], and to complain to [regulator, e.g., the California Privacy Protection Agency or the competent German state data protection authority]. If you have any questions, contact [privacy desk email].

Deliver securely: an encrypted portal, or a password-protected file with the password sent separately; paper only by tracked courier; never to an unverified personal email. Use a commonly used electronic format where the law requires (GDPR Art. 15(3); CCPA portability).

No charge, except where the law allows a reasonable fee for manifestly unfounded, excessive or repeat requests; California personnel-file copies may be charged at the actual cost of reproduction, and Washington copies are free.
A second reviewer checks the redactions, checks the response against the request, and confirms that no one else's data or privileged material is included.
Close the ticket with the dates (received, acknowledged, extended, responded), systems searched, exemptions applied, reviewer and a copy of the response.

Keep request records for at least 24 months (CCPA regulations) and per the retention schedule elsewhere, without keeping extra copies of the disclosed data beyond what's needed to evidence the response.
Report volume by type and country, on-time rate, median days and refusals to the Privacy Office every quarter.
Send recurring gaps in systems, retention or notices to DS-03 and HR Technology for fixing.

notes: Any request is a request: it doesn't need to cite a law, use a form or reach the privacy desk directly, so train managers and HRBPs to forward requests within 1 business day.
Set the deadline at intake from the shortest applicable regime. A California employee's payroll records (21 days) and personnel file (30 days) fall due before the CCPA's 45 days.
In disputes, an access request is often discovery by another route. Involve Legal early, but don't let the dispute delay a statutory response.
Redact consistently and log every withholding decision with its legal basis. Over-redaction invites regulator complaints; under-redaction breaches other people's privacy.
Investigation files need special care: protect complainants and witnesses, withhold privileged material, and disclose the requester's own data where the law requires.
The response package is itself sensitive personal data, so deliver it securely and keep evidence of exactly what was sent.

countryNotes.us: There is no federal employee access right, but many states grant personnel-file inspection with deadlines (e.g., IL, MN, OR, MA, MI, CT), so route those through the same desk and apply the local deadline.
countryNotes.us-ca: CCPA rights to know, delete, correct and limit cover employees, applicants and contractors (45 days, extendable by 45). Personnel files are due within 30 days (LC 1198.5, including training records under SB 513) and payroll records within 21 days (LC 226), each with $750 penalties.
countryNotes.us-co: The Colorado Privacy Act doesn't cover HR data. Current employees may inspect and copy their personnel file at least once a year, and former employees once after separation (C.R.S. 8-2-129).
countryNotes.us-nc: North Carolina gives employees and applicants no statutory access, correction or deletion rights, so handle requests under company policy or other states' laws.
countryNotes.us-tx: The TDPSA excludes employment data and there is no personnel-file right, so handle requests under policy; respond separately to subpoenas and TWC requests for payroll records.
countryNotes.us-wa: HB 1308 gives employees and former employees (for 3 years) free personnel-file copies and a signed discharge-reason statement within 21 days, with statutory damages of $250-$1,000. Employees may request corrections once a year and add rebuttals.
countryNotes.ca: BC PIPA gives employees access rights, handled by the privacy officer within 30 days (verify business-day counting); PIPEDA covers commercial data. Ontario private-sector employees have no statutory access right, but apply a consistent 30-day standard, and Quebec Law 25 covers any Quebec remote staff.
countryNotes.de: GDPR access requests are due within 1 month (extendable by 2) with a copy of the data; they are routinely used as leverage in termination disputes, and failures lead to Art. 82 damages claims. Employees also have a separate personnel-file inspection right (§83 BetrVG), and BDSG §§29 and 34 allow limited refusals.
countryNotes.il: Protection of Privacy Law ss.13-14 give access and correction rights within the regulatory period (verify the days), and Amendment 13 adds statutory damages of up to NIS 10,000 for some failures. Employees can also obtain payroll and attendance records through the Labor Court.
countryNotes.in: Until 13 May 2027 the SPDI Rules require a grievance officer; from then, the DPDP Act gives access, correction, erasure and grievance rights answered within 90 days. Processing for employment under s.7(i) still carries these rights.
countryNotes.tw: The PDPA gives rights to inquire, review, obtain copies, correct, stop processing and delete; access requests are generally due within 15 days and correction or deletion within 30, each extendable once (verify). Respond in Traditional Chinese.
countryNotes.cn: PIPL Arts. 44-47 give rights to access, copy, correct, delete and port data, and refusals must give reasons (Art. 50). There is no fixed deadline, so target 15 working days (verify), and keep response data in China unless a transfer basis exists.
countryNotes.vn: Under the PDPL and Decree 356, acknowledge within 2 working days and complete within 10 days (access, correction), 15 days (restriction, withdrawal) or 20 days (deletion). Employees can also ask for copies of documents about their working history at termination (LC Art. 48(3)).
